verdict.reason: The file clearly shows sentence 15 marks "There" with role="M" (Modifier) in the There-be construction "There is rarely a perfect level, only trade-offs to be balanced." This is incorrect. In standard English grammar, "There" in There-be constructions is a dummy/formal subject (형식주어), not a modifier. It has no semantic content and exists only to occupy the subject position. The role should not be "M" but rather "S" (as a formal subject) or noted distinctly as a dummy subject. The claim that "There는 형식주어(dummy subject)이나, 현재 M(Modifier)으로 표기됨" is factually accurate—this is a real annotation error in the JSON file.

verdict.reason: The grammar_note at page3 > sentences[14] (line 539) incorrectly labels "to be balanced" as part of a "There is + 동격(to be p.p.)" construction. However, "to be balanced" does not function as an appositive (which would rename/restate the noun). Instead, it is a postpositive to-infinitive phrase modifying "trade-offs" — it specifies what action must be taken regarding the trade-offs. The correct structure is "There is + noun + 후치수식(postpositive modifier)" not appositive. The critical distinction: appositives rename (A, B = same thing), while postpositive modifiers qualify/constrain (what property/action applies to the noun).
